main_body: A flat dark-green ground patch (4x3 tiles) with sparse repeated tufts, scattered brown, red and gold specks. There is no standing volume.
top_band: none; this is a flat terrain surface with no top and front structure, and a column read gives only dark green ground with occasional tuft or speck pixels
evidence: The candidate is a seamless ground texture, not a standing object. The 3/4 top-and-front contract does not apply, and no wrong-projection pattern is drawn (no elevation, slab or rim). The small tuft shapes have a tiny lighter cap and dark base, but they are details on a ground surface. Terrain kind matches, so the 3/4 check is not applicable and the piece is treated as passing Part A.

style.evidence: The ground is built from about 3 close dark-green steps (base, slightly darker blotches, tuft highlights) plus a few sparse accent pixels in brown, red and gold. The base is a nearly flat dark green with only a faint grid-like checker, and large areas show no grain. The repeating tuft/speck motif is identical every 8 tiles, which looks mechanical. Next to the Beodeul grass and paving, which have 5-6 steps, per-clump texture and varied tiles, it is thinner and less information-rich per tile, mostly 3-5 colours.
